author: Contributor 87
about: Tidewater Yoga's Discord: Maya's own helper bot builds the server and answers on the Gateway, Scheduler posts the week's schedule, Cal.com announces bookings; and Open Autonomy's project server, where the kit's setup checks its bot and home channel and the project's agent answers on the Gateway, first Hermes (reconciling its slash commands with the application's as it starts, then reacting, threading and editing its answer), then Volter Harness (journeys/customer-life.outline.md). Aaron also uses the registered /status and /usage commands: Hermes privately defers, edits or deletes the original acknowledgement, then resolves a confirmation with a callback and token-scoped followup.

It sets its status: watching the schedule
On start it asks for the website's invite: Discord answers the same one

Tuesday 13 January
Act 11: Aaron, who maintains Open Autonomy at Volter, has a Discord account
He creates the project's server "Open Autonomy" in the client
In the Developer Portal he makes the application under the project's branding, "Open Autonomy", and turns on the Message Content intent Hermes needs
He adds the bot to the server with the portal's install link: view, send, read history, react, open threads and send in them
Before the kit, Aaron tries the application from a scratch script, as Discord's application-commands page shows: it registers /ping

body.name: status
body.description: Is the bot up?

steps.name: He runs the kit's setup with the discord door: it reads the bot's application and checks it against the project's branding
For DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL he copied the server's id, not the channel's: setup reads it and Discord knows no such channel, so setup stops
He copies #general's id and runs setup again: the home channel is a server channel
The kit starts Hermes's gateway: discord.py logs in with the token setup saved, reading the bot's own user
…and its application, with its owner
Hermes opens the Gateway at Discord's own host (gateway.discord.gg): HELLO
It identifies with discord.py's default intents, message content and voice states: READY, then the server
Once READY, Hermes reconciles its slash commands, as it does on every start: it lists the application's global commands and finds the two of Aaron's script
/ping is none of Hermes's: it deletes it first
It creates /new, the first of its commands the application lacks, 4.5 seconds apart

Reloading MCP servers invalidates the prompt cache, so Hermes asks in #general first: the prompt as text and as an embed, with Approve Once, Always Approve and Cancel

embeds.description:
⚠️ **Confirm /reload-mcp**

Reloading MCP servers rebuilds the tool set for this session and **invalidates the provider prompt cache** — the next message will re-send full input tokens.  On long-context or high-reasoning models this can be expensive.

Choose:
• **Approve Once** — reload now
• **Always Approve** — reload now and silence this prompt permanently
• **Cancel** — leave MCP tools unchanged

_Text fallback: reply `/approve`, `/always`, or `/cancel`._
embeds.title: /reload-mcp
